# Pull Request Template

### Description
Please provide a brief summary of the changes you've made, the problem this addresses, and any context that helps explain your approach. 

As a general rule, we prefer to keep our pull requests small and focused. Each merge should address one specific thing rather than bundling a lot of different changes together. This keeps the review process smooth and drastically reduces the risk of breaking existing functionality.

### Related Issues
Fixes # (issue number)

### Visual Evidence
Every pull request is reviewed by the team, and having a visual reference makes a massive difference. If your changes affect the UI or change any workflows, please include screenshots or GIFs demonstrating your updates so we can clearly see what changed.

| Before | After / Demo |
| :--- | :--- |
| *Add image/GIF* | *Add image/GIF* |

### Type of Change
- Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to behave unexpectedly)
- Refactoring, chore, or documentation update

### Checklist
- My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- I have performed a self-review of my own changes
- I have commented on sections of code that might be complex or hard to follow
- My changes do not introduce any new warnings

### A Quick Note on Merging
Just a heads-up that we prefer squash merges for all pull requests to keep our main branch history clean and easy to follow. Please make sure your branch commits are clear, as they will be bundled together during the merge.
